subject: Logic
title: Mary's Room
description: A short lesson to help you apply Mary's Room.

hook.text: Mary knows every scientific fact about color but has lived her entire life in a black-and-white room. She steps outside.

buildup.text: Frank Jackson proposed this in 1982: does Mary learn something new when she sees red for the first time?

discovery.text: If she does, then physical facts alone don't capture everything—subjective experience adds something beyond data.

twist.text: Physicalists argue she doesn't learn a new fact—she just gains a new ability, like recognizing red by sight.

climax.text: The debate cuts to the heart of consciousness: is experience reducible to information, or is there something more?

punchline.text: Knowing everything about red ≠ seeing red.

quiz.question: What does Mary's Room challenge?
options: Whether physical facts fully explain subjective experience
